dogecoin.text: @MStiive @lexfridman @VitalikButerin @ethereum @Bitcoin @dogecoin @elonmusk @ShibainuCoin @IOHK_Charles @Cardano @chainlink @0xPolygon @Truebitprotocol likewise. Just like you, just doing my best to understand the tech.

@MStiive @lexfridman @VitalikButerin @ethereum @Bitcoin @dogecoin @elonmusk @ShibainuCoin @IOHK_Charles @Cardano @chainlink @0xPolygon @Truebitprotocol My main point is being missed. If the verification game inherit in Truebit is not required, due to the use of ZK proofs, then solvers/ verifiers are not required. Does Truebit pivot to replace solver/ verifier with ZKP ? I dont know.

@MStiive @lexfridman @VitalikButerin @ethereum @Bitcoin @dogecoin @elonmusk @ShibainuCoin @IOHK_Charles @Cardano @chainlink @0xPolygon @Truebitprotocol The concept is that POW is to show work was done to arrive at an answer. Decentralisation ensures the answer is correct ( everyone checks everyones work). Off chain computation reduces the amount of work to go on chain. Verification is required. Verifiers Dilemma is the problem.

@MStiive @lexfridman @VitalikButerin @ethereum @Bitcoin @dogecoin @elonmusk @ShibainuCoin @IOHK_Charles @Cardano @chainlink @0xPolygon @Truebitprotocol Thats absolutely a fair comment. There is no malice in my use of  $TRU to frame the question, its just the tokenomics model that I understand best in the space of challenge games/ verifiers dilemma.

@MStiive @lexfridman @VitalikButerin @ethereum @Bitcoin @dogecoin @elonmusk @ShibainuCoin @IOHK_Charles @Cardano @chainlink @0xPolygon @Truebitprotocol I believe its overall network effect + security of Ethereum that will keep ZK on chain, rather than side or centralised etc.

ZK solutions are proofs, as opposed to verification games - yes also computationally heavy, but done off chain, only the proof (answer) goes on chain.

@SheldonStack @MStiive @lexfridman @VitalikButerin @ethereum @Bitcoin @dogecoin @elonmusk @ShibainuCoin @IOHK_Charles @Cardano @chainlink @0xPolygon @Truebitprotocol A role yes, but perhaps only for a season. ZK tech is moving so fast, if it solves the verifiers dilemma, replaces 'challenge games', then $TRU may fade before it shines. Would like to be proven where I am wrong, as up to now, a big $TRU supporter.

@MStiive @lexfridman @VitalikButerin @ethereum @Bitcoin @dogecoin @elonmusk @ShibainuCoin @IOHK_Charles @Cardano @chainlink @0xPolygon @Truebitprotocol The argument supporting decentralisation seems to win here. Centralisation has had several hundred years to prove its limitations.
To me, the question is not about replacing DLT, its how best we solve trustless verification. I had hoped $TRU was that, now, not so sure.
